record.paper_title: Seven open problems in applied combinatorics
record.original_question: Consider a 4-uniform hypergraph H=(V,E) with source node s and sink node t. In the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem, one must separate s and t while minimizing the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits and forbidding any 2-vs-2 hyperedge splits. Determine the computational complexity of this problem.

evidence.quote: This limit converges to the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem: minimize the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits when separating s and t, without making any 2-vs-2 hyperedge splits.
Open Problem 3.2. What is the complexity of the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H = (V, E) be a 4-uniform hypergraph (every hyperedge contains exactly four vertices) with two distinguished vertices s, t ∈ V. Given a bipartition (S, V \ S) with s ∈ S and t ∈ V \ S, each hyperedge e ∈ E is classified by how its four vertices split between S and V \ S as 4-vs-0, 3-vs-1, or 2-vs-2. Call the bipartition admissible if no hyperedge is split 2-vs-2 (i.e., every hyperedge has all four endpoints on the same side, or exactly one endpoint on one side and three on the other). The No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem asks, among all admissible bipartitions separating s from t, for one minimizing the number of hyperedges that are split 1-vs-3. 

Determine the computational complexity of this problem: is it polynomial-time solvable, NP-hard, or otherwise classified?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on cardinality-based minimum s-t cut problems in hypergraphs establishes that the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem is NP-hard, via a reduction from maximum cut. This resolves the complexity question by showing the problem is intractable (assuming P ≠ NP).

status_evidence.title: Improved Hardness Results of the Cardinality-Based Minimum s-t Cut Problem in Hypergraphs
status_evidence.snippet: For 4-uniform hypergraphs with w_2 ∈ [0,1), the problem is NP-hard by reduction from maximum cut; the No-Even-Split limit lies in this regime.
status_evidence.claim: NP-hardness of the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem is established by reduction from MaxCut.
